raw_answer_text:
A1: The switch learns from the source address of every frame it receives — the flow shows `learn` (source-MAC learning) happening for every frame before the destination lookup, independent of whether the destination is found.
A2: It associates the frame's source MAC address (SA) with the ingress port on which the frame arrived.
A3: Whether an entry for the destination MAC is found in the MAC table ("Entry found?"): if found (hit=yes) and the egress port differs from the ingress port, the switch forwards out that single port; if not found, it floods.
A4: The switch floods it to all ports in the VLAN, and the port that is always excluded is the ingress port (the port the frame arrived on).
A5: NOT STATED as an explicit rule in the labeled model, but a comment notes both unknown unicast and broadcast/multicast destinations are treated the same way — both result in flooding.
A6: It filters (discards) the frame when the destination entry is found in the table but its learned egress port is the same as the ingress port.
A7: NOT STATED explicitly, though once the destination is learned ("Entry found?" = yes) the switch stops flooding and instead either forwards it out the single learned port or filters it, depending on whether that learned port equals the ingress port.
A8: NOT STATED.
